fixtures.label: One product, four movement types — the 5-column Reference arm
fixtures.description:
The only fixture rendering the CONDITIONAL Reference column — the 5-column arm, where `checkout-no-reference` is the 4-column floor. `hasReference` is `items.some((i) => i.reference)` and the two fixtures cover its two answers; a template that hard-coded the column would pass on this one alone. It also pins `itemColumnCount = 4 + 1`, which `edgeColumn` derives the page's second alignment edge from — so a column-count regression moves the #details block as well as the grid.

⭐ The only fixture reaching all FOUR movement types in one document — `prep`, `check_out`, `check_in`, `mark_lost` (movements 877, 879, 881, 882). That is what exercises `actionLabel`, the generic transform the template carries deliberately instead of a lookup table in `@cfs/core` (the manager's `MovementTimeline.tsx` writes the same `startCase(camelCase(t))`, so `check_in` must read "Check In" on both surfaces). A one- or two-type session leaves most of it unrendered.

⚠️ THE TWO WRITERS DIFFER, WHICH IS WHY BOTH CAPTURES ARE KEPT. This is a `journal-migration` reconstruction: `created_by.name` is "Journal Migration" rather than a person, and the cutover wrote a sentence into `reference` on EVERY row. The live check-out path writes `reference: ""` — that is `checkout-no-reference`. The pair covers both the column arm and both writers; neither is a near-duplicate.

It is also the only fixture whose quantities deliberately do not reconcile line-to-line: 30 prepped and checked out, 25 checked back in, 5 marked lost. A receipt states what changed hands per movement rather than a net, so the partial return and the loss are two rows, not one adjustment — an edit that starts netting them goes red here.

Captured from prod session `83bf4176-a4d2-8646-8b1d-5652cf3b5d1c` (order 893, one product, 90 units over 4 rows). Single order, so `showOrderBanner` is FALSE here and the banner arm is not covered — it has no prod carrier and is hand-authored beside these.

fixtures.label: Nine products checked out — the 4-column floor, live writer
fixtures.description:
The 4-column FLOOR: `reference` is `""` on all 18 rows, so `hasReference` is false and the grid is exactly Item Description / Action / Qty / Movement #. Its partner is `lifecycle-with-loss`, the 5-column arm; the two cover both answers of the one conditional this template has, and neither substitutes. The floor also pins the OTHER value of `edgeColumn` — `itemColumnCount` is 4 here and 5 there, so the page's second alignment edge sits in a different place in each, and #details is checked against both.

⭐ It is the LIVE writer, where the partner is a migration reconstruction, and that is the second reason to keep both. `created_by.name` is a real operator (masked on capture), the checkout path wrote `reference: ""` rather than a sentence, and every `check_out` row carries a real `lines[].location` pair while every `prep` row carries `lines: []`. So this is the document that shows the ordinary shape production writes today; the partner shows what the journal cutover left behind, and that population does not grow.

It is also the family's only MULTI-PRODUCT and only long grid — 9 products, 18 rows, 280 units — so it is what puts the items table under enough vertical pressure to show row rhythm and header treatment, where the partner is 4 rows. Deliberately still one page: the page-break case belongs in its own fixture if one is ever wanted.

⚠️ Single order (1007), so `showOrderBanner` is FALSE here too. No prod session spans orders — measured — so the banner and the `null`-organization arms have no capture available and are hand-authored beside these, each saying in its own description why it is synthetic.

Captured from prod session `b2b50277-377d-4585-b69c-6eaff89f7a73`, a `prep` + `check_out` pair per product on 2026-08-27.

fixtures.label: Three group banners, one customer — SYNTHETIC
fixtures.description:
SYNTHETIC, and it has to be: measured 2026-09-08, NO prod movement session spans orders, so `showOrderBanner` (`groups.length > 1`) is false in every capture available and the whole banner half of the grid is rendered by nothing. Do not "clean it up" into a capture — there is nothing to capture. It is still the driving case for the surface it comes from: `POST /returns` accepts whatever a worker was handed back, so an item from order A returned beside order B is the design, not a data fault.

It covers FOUR things no capture reaches, in one document because they co-occur in the real shape:
1. THE ORDER BANNER, with `it.sessions.sessionQuantity` per group — 18 / 14 / 5 against a document total of 37, so a banner summing the wrong rows is visible rather than plausible.
2. THE `null`-ORDER GROUP, rendering "No order". A manual movement swept into a session is still something the customer was handed, so it is banner-ed rather than dropped.
3. THE PLURAL in #details — "Order Numbers:", `orders.length > 1`. Every capture renders the singular.
4. THE FILENAME's OTHER ARM. `render.filename` is `Receipt<% if (orders.length === 1) { %> - Order N<% } %> - <date>`, so a multi-order session drops the number. That conditional had a fixture on neither side until this pair.

⚠️ Not run through `applyPii` — there is no capture to run — so every masked leaf is written by hand from `@cfs/core/utils/fixture-pii`'s own vocabularies: the organization from `FAKE_ORGANIZATIONS`, the worker from `FAKE_FIRST_NAMES`/`FAKE_LAST_NAMES`. Keep it that way when editing; the fixture-PII guard has no carve-out for hand-built fixtures, deliberately — a carve-out is exactly where a real name would hide.

Its partner is `anonymous-cross-customer`: the same cross-order shape with `organization: null`, so the diff between the two goldens is the letterhead's customer-name line and nothing else.
